title: Grateful Dead Live at Labor Temple on 1969-02-02
lineage: SBD > MR > ? > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with uneven mix but strong early‑69 psychedelic performance – highlights include a soaring Dark Star, blistering Eleven and fiery Lovelight.
ai_review.review: The show captures the Dead at a creative peak in early ’69, delivering classic psychedelia with Dark Star, The Eleven, Turn On Your Lovelight and an intense Other One>Cryptical sequence. While the SBD source is historically valuable, listeners note a thin low‑end, occasional splice and a noticeable cut in The Eleven that detract from an otherwise vivid listening experience.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is ~4.4 stars; most comments praise the musical performance despite consistent complaints about mix balance, leading to a strong overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Uneven and sometimes thin mix – low‑end is weak, Jerry’s guitar sits high in the spectrum. Notable splice in GMLSG and a cut/fade in The Eleven. Overall above‑average for a 1969 tape but not pristine.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑69 psychedelic set that launches straight into high‑energy material, with tight transitions and a concise seven‑song arc that showcases the band’s improvisational peak.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for inspired, focused guitar solos and a powerful amp‑driven tone; his playing is described as the centerpiece of the show.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s harmonica/organ shines on Turn On Your Lovelight and Good Mornin' Little Schoolgirl, adding soulful grit to the set.
